title: AI Agent Weekly #2: Robinhood Opens the Floodgates — AI Agents Now Trade Stocks

sections.title: 🔥 Top Story
sections.content: **Robinhood now lets your AI agents trade stocks.** The fintech giant opened API access for autonomous AI trading agents this week, letting models place buy/sell orders, monitor portfolios, and rebalance — all without human intervention. The HN thread exploded to 180 comments as developers debated the implications: algorithmic trading was already automated, but this puts AI agent reasoning directly on the trade execution path. Our analysis: this is the first major consumer fintech to explicitly endorse agent-driven trading. Expect a wave of 'AI hedge fund in a box' startups, followed by regulatory scrutiny. The question isn't whether agents will trade — it's who bears liability when they lose money.

sections.title: 💡 Business Model Spotlight
sections.content: **Agent Skills Marketplaces are the next app store.** GitHub saw 72 new agent-related repos in the past 7 days — and the fastest-growing ones aren't frameworks. They're *skills*. DannyMac180/skills (⭐315) is a curated collection of reusable AI agent skills. nihaixia-tcm (⭐187) packages Traditional Chinese Medicine knowledge as an agent skill. Metamask-openclaw (⭐246) wraps crypto wallet operations for agents. The pattern is clear: developers are building composable, domain-specific agent capabilities that anyone can plug into their workflow. The monetization play? Build a marketplace of vetted agent skills with usage-based pricing. Whoever owns the skill distribution channel owns the agent economy.

sections.title: 🤑 Monetization Tip
sections.content: **Build agent skills, not agents.** The gold rush isn't in building yet another agent framework — it's in building the skills those agents use. A weather-checking skill, a crypto-wallet skill, a PDF-parsing skill, a TCM diagnosis skill — these are the 'micro-SaaS' of 2026. Each skill is a $9-29/month subscription. Package 5 domain-specific skills together and you have a $99/month B2B product. The barrier is low (a single well-crafted system prompt + an API wrapper), but the market is wide open. Start with industries where domain expertise is rare: legal, medical, tax, and compliance.
